text:
elena: heads up — after the runtime deploy we pushed last night I'm seeing a regression on the paged-attn path. p95 spikes and KV pager churn increases when the batcher picks adaptive grouping. :eyes:

elena: quick profile snippet from the staging repro:
```
PROFILE req=conv-1234
model=galactica-3b
kernel=flash-fused-v2
batcher=adaptive-token-group
latency_p50=18ms p95=120ms
kv_pages_alloc=324 frag_bytes=47MB
pager_evictions_per_s=14
```

elena: tracer shows a lot of short-lived page pins around the fused kernel exec. looks like fused path pins larger contiguous buffers which triggers evictions on our paged allocator.

mike: can you repro deterministically? is it sequence-length mix dependent or request ordering?

elena: repro with mixed seqs (8/64/256) and bursty arrival. if I force grouping by token_count the selector picks fused and pager churns. if I force grouping by max_seq it picks the non-fused flash variant.

prasanna: this matches my bench. when batcher groups different seqs into one call, kernel_selector scores fused highly because of better arithmetic intensity, but fused grabs a big contiguous KV scratch which our block-table allocator currently maps to multiple page ranges and causes fragmentation.

prasanna: small mitigation experiment: pin to flash-no-fuse in runtime and keep adaptive batching -> p95 drops back down and pager_evictions/sec -> 2. quick numbers in staging:
```
baseline (adaptive+fused): p95=120ms evict/s=14
force-no-fuse: p95=34ms evict/s=2
old-batcher(max_seq): p95=32ms evict/s=1.5
```

jordan: so there are two interacting components: batcher heuristics and kernel memory layout. allocator needs to prefer contiguous placements for fused kernels or batcher should avoid cross-seq grouping that triggers fused choice.

mike: agree. which is the faster/safer rollback? change kernel scoring or tweak batcher grouping?

elena: immediate fix = runtime env hint to avoid fused for paged-attn while we iterate on allocator. patch ready to flip via config. longer term: either make block-table allocations coalesce for fused's buffer shapes or add kernel-memory-cost to selector scoring.

prasanna: i started a small prototype to annotate kernel descriptors with an "alloc_profile" (contiguous / scatter / small_objects) and pass that to pager allocator. if alloc_profile == contiguous we try to reserve slab-aligned ranges to avoid splitting. initial microbench shows 40% fewer evictions.

jordan: nice. also add a counter in telemetry: kernel_chosen + kv_page_faults_per_request so we can correlate in prod.

infra-bot: deploybot: rolled back runtime flag for fused kernels on paged-attn in staging at 2026-03-17T09:12:05Z (v1.48.3 -> v1.48.2).

mike: action items:
- elena: push the runtime flag to prod-safe rollout (canary 10%)
- prasanna: finish alloc_profile prototype + perf test by EOD tomorrow
- jordan: add telemetry metric and dashboard for kernel vs kv-pager evictions

elena: I'll open the rollout PR and link the staging traces. will also add the reproduction script in the ticket. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks team. next sync we can decide whether to change batcher heuristics or kernel selector scoring based on alloc_profile results.

elena: attaching the repro command for anyone who wants to run locally:
```bash
# repro script (staging credentials required)
python tools/repro/paged_attn_repro.py --model galactica-3b --mix 8,64,256 --burst 50 --duration 60
```

prasanna: running now, will post logs if I see anything else.

jordan: FYI I put a note in the kernel-selector docs about memory-profile diminishing returns for fused on paged allocators. not a long-term doc, just a pointer.

elena: cool. thanks all.
